title: Physicochemical Properties of Torus Mandibularis and Palatinus Indicate a Source of Autogenous Bone Graft Martin
authors: Luis S. Redor, Rui Zhang, Natthamet Wongsirichat, Ratchapin Laovanitch Srisatjaluk, Teeranut Chaiyasamut, Dutmanee Seriwatanachai. Open Dentistry Journal. Vol.15, No.1 (2021), 357-365. DOI 10.2174/1874210602115010357
supports: Pre-clinical study from the botiss cerabone (sintered bovine bone) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Tori bone was different from bone graft substitutes in terms of surface structure, crystallinity, and calcium release. However, tori bone and bone graft substitutes were similar in terms of elemental composition and crystal compounds, which may positively affect their clinical applications. Taken together, our findings suggest that with an effective decontamination, tori bone should be considered as a viable material for bone grafting, as it is not only practical but also cost-efficient for patients” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
